name: Off-Highway Vehicle
description: A vehicle designed or adapted for cross-country travel over unimproved terrain, ice or snow, which its owner declares at registration, and the DMV finds, unsuitable for general highway use, such as an electric dirt bike. Defined by 13 AAC 40.010(a)(30), with its highway rules in 13 AAC 02.430 to 02.455 and its registration fee in Alaska Statutes §28.10.421.
restrictions: Designed or adapted for cross-country travel over unimproved terrain, ice or snow, and declared unsuitable for general highway use when registered
No limit on motor power or speed
May be registered with the DMV as an off-highway vehicle for $10, $20 or $30 for two, four or six years, with a numbered decal
A two-wheeled dirt bike or off-road motorcycle can't be registered as an all-purpose vehicle, the class of ATV allowed on some low-speed community roads

Not ridden on a highway's roadway or shoulder, except to cross it or a bridge or culvert, when snow or ice keeps other traffic off, when the road is posted open to off-highway vehicles, or when the road authority allows it
May ride a highway right-of-way outside the roadway and shoulder, at least three feet from the roadway's edge, but not on a controlled-access highway or in a divided highway's median
Crosses a highway at roughly a right angle, after a complete stop, yielding to all traffic
Never on sidewalks, paths for pedestrians or other nonmotorized traffic, alleys, or vehicular ways or areas not open to off-highway vehicles
Carries a passenger on a highway only when built with a seat for one

Allowed without a permit on state public domain land, on or off an established road easement, when its curb weight is 1,500 lb or less, as long as riding off the easement causes no significant rutting, ground disturbance, drainage changes, thermal erosion or water quality damage
In state parks, a rider under 14 must be accompanied and directly supervised by a parent or someone 21 or older
State park regulations' off-road vehicle needs more than one drive wheel or track, so a two-wheeled dirt e-moto isn't one there
